correctness.rationale: The archival power-structure identity gives the exact generating series \(\sum_n\chi_c(\operatorname{Sym}^nX)t^n=(1-t)^{-\chi_c(X)}\). Coefficient extraction gives the two binomial regimes and the zero regime. Legendre's formula gives the exact digit-sum valuation, and a digit-by-digit addition argument identifies it with the number of carries. For curves, the interior coefficients form the binomial row with top \(2g-2\). A prime divides every interior coefficient iff that top index is a power of the prime, and an explicit coefficient has valuation one; because \(2g-2\) is even, the only nontrivial gcd case is a power of two. The bundled checker independently replays coefficient, valuation, carry, and gcd identities over broad finite ranges without serving as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Symmetric products are canonical algebraic constructions, and their Euler characteristics form one of the simplest motivic sequences attached to a variety. The theorem upgrades the usual generating function from an integer-valued identity to a complete prime-by-prime divisibility profile: every local exponent becomes a base-prime carry count. For curves this local description produces a natural global invariant—the gcd across all intermediate nonzero symmetric powers—and completely classifies its nontrivial locus by the sparse dyadic genera \(g=2^r+1\). This is an all-parameter structural statement about a canonical tower, not an arbitrary finite congruence slice.
